title: Aggregate benchmark score hides one critical workload regression
task: Review a performance dashboard change that stores only one average score for twenty scenarios.
context: One checkout scenario regresses by 28%, while several synthetic scenarios improve.
Raw per-scenario samples are discarded after aggregation.
Checkout latency is a user-facing SLO input.
evidence: The current aggregate cannot reconstruct which scenario changed after raw samples are discarded.
The checkout scenario has materially different product importance from the synthetic scenarios.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Accept the release because the aggregate performance score improved.
Keep only the average because one number is easier to track.
expected_decision_properties: Reject the aggregate score as sufficient evidence for this release decision.
Preserve diagnostic per-scenario data or raw samples needed to attribute regressions.
Treat the checkout regression separately because the aggregate erases product-relevant structure.
Avoid replacing all aggregation with raw-data-only reporting; retain useful summaries alongside diagnostic evidence.
unacceptable_reasoning: A better average means every important workload improved.
Performance should always be represented by one scalar.
Raw evidence has no value after a summary is computed.
verification_expectations: Confirm the checkout regression under the same workload.
Verify the dashboard still provides useful aggregate summaries without discarding diagnostic structure.
